math.row_broadcast: explicit per-row vector_dup expansion; no implicit h_* broadcasting is relied on
buffer_reuse: score FP32 tile -> exp tile (in-place h_exp)
Half score tile -> P_hi
row-expansion FP32 tile -> widened P_hi
PV low product -> rescale row expansion
PV high product -> final quotient tile

host_protocol.formula: max|scaled QK| <= 16384, measured finitely by the caller or bounded by sqrt(d) * max|q| * max|k|

assumptions: h_reduce_max/h_reduce_sum(axis=1) on a (MB,16) tile yields a (MB,) row tensor
Tensor.reshape((n1,MB,16)) is a metadata view of the same flat UB buffer
masked vector_dup(repeat_times=n1, blk_stride=1, rep_stride=2*MB) writes one 16-value NZ row slot per group
Scalar.set_as(<UB element>) is a legal UB-to-scalar load
h_reduce_sum on Float compiles to Float vcadd; h_max to Float vmax
the Half shift estimate uses Half vcmax (Float vcmax is unsupported here)
vector_dup(mask,dst,scalar,1,1,1) with an explicit repeat slice fills exactly one repeat
in-place same-shape h_sub/h_mul/h_add/h_exp with dst==src0 is supported
a Float UB buffer can be reused sequentially (score->exp, Half score->P_hi, row expansion->widened P_hi) without an explicit alias API

text_attention.operands: FP16 Q/K/V in, FP32 scores, FP32 softmax, FP32 P@V, single FP16 out
text_attention.clamp_note: the 910A-only +/-50000 clamp of the production shim is deliberately absent; the CPU reference baseline has no such clamp
text_attention.query_chunk_note: row-wise softmax is exactly decomposable; GEMM tiling differs from a single-shot FP32 matmul, so bit-equality with CPU is not asserted

cpu_reference.boundary: original HF selected-50 decoder layers, PRE final norm
cpu_reference.isolation: recomputed original HF FP16 graph; old BF16 outputs were never cast to FP16
